description: The Geometry half of the built-in-names rule, checked with Core Language alone: `define grid ... end` raises `ol-reserved-word` even though the `geometry` profile is NOT active. `spec/grammar.md:408` is why -- "a name that could be declared in one implementation but not in another would be invisible and unpredictable to a learner", so what a profile decides is whether a name WORKS, never whether a program may declare it -- and `:414` makes the built-in names "exactly the keywords listed above plus every primitive", `grid` among them. Its profile-ACTIVE counterparts are `reserved-word-define-axes` (the same `define`/`end` shape over another Geometry primitive) and `reserved-word-struct-grid` (this same name in the `struct` slot): all three raise, which is the point -- the profile set is not a discriminating variable for this question, and it takes the group to prove that rather than any one of them. `"check": true`: this is a checker rule and nothing executes. `message` is deliberately absent from the diagnostics below: the harness strips it from BOTH sides before comparing (`scripts/harness/index.mjs:977-983` projects every diagnostic to code/span/params/stage/severity), so supplying one here would be an assertion nothing can evaluate. Diagnostic identity is `code` plus `params` and "prose is presentation" (`spec/error-model.md:254-259`); the learner-facing wording is pinned by unit tests instead. Its two counterparts omit `message` as well, so nothing here is asymmetric.
